_meta.what: One scene written both ways. The BEFORE side is read out of git, never retyped, so the comparison cannot drift.
_meta.why: The WORDS lane brief (Paolo 8/26): "one scene rewritten both ways, side by side, so the difference is visible instead of described."
_meta.note: Both columns are drafts. Nothing here is put to him for approval; every line is editable in the WORDS tab and the words are his.

rules.1: THEY TALK LIKE THEY ARE IN A HURRY
rules.3: SOMEBODY HAS TO ASK, SOMEBODY HAS TO FUMBLE
rules.5: NAME THE ONE THING ONLY THIS PERSON WOULD NAME
rules.6: THE LINE IS NOT THE POINT

pairs.speaker: JOURNAL
pairs.before: The block loses half its light at the same hour every night.
pairs.after: Nine at night, every night, half this block goes brown.

pairs.speaker: JOURNAL
pairs.before: The line tests clean. A clean line that browns out is a shared one. Found the split.
pairs.after: Line tests clean. Clean and browning out means somebody's on our feed. Found the split.

pairs.speaker: JOURNAL
pairs.before: Put the current back myself. The block has light tonight. Nobody was told.
pairs.after: Put the current back myself. Block has light tonight. Nobody knows it was me.

pairs.speaker: JOURNAL
pairs.before: Handed the tap to the trades. They patched it in daylight, names on the work order.
pairs.after: Handed the tap to the trades. Daylight patch, every name on the work order.

pairs.speaker: JOURNAL
pairs.before: Cut the skim line in front of the whole block. Sparks, a crowd, and a message sent up.
pairs.after: Cut the skim line in front of the whole block. Sparks, a crowd, and somebody upstream has my face now.

pairs.speaker: JOURNAL
pairs.before: Left it alone. The block goes dark again tonight, same hour.
pairs.after: Left it alone. Block goes dark again tonight, same hour.

pairs.speaker: lineman
pairs.before: Every night, same hour, this block loses half its light.
pairs.after: Nine at night. Every night, nine, and half this block goes brown.

pairs.speaker: lineman
pairs.before: The line tests clean. A clean line that browns out is not a broken line. It is a shared one.
pairs.after: I tested it myself. Line's clean. Clean and browning out means somebody upstream is on my feed drinking before we do.

pairs.speaker: lineman
pairs.before: Somebody upstream is drinking before we do. Walk it back for me. Quiet, if you can manage quiet.
pairs.after: So walk it back for me. Past the dead storefronts, follow whatever cable's running warm. You any good at quiet?

pairs.speaker: PLAYER
pairs.before: I will walk it back.
pairs.after: I'll walk it.

pairs.speaker: PLAYER
pairs.before: Why not walk it yourself?
pairs.after: Why not you?

pairs.speaker: PLAYER
pairs.before: Not my block.
pairs.after: Not my block.

pairs.speaker: PLAYER
pairs.before: (say nothing, just go)
pairs.after: (say nothing, just go)

pairs.speaker: lineman
pairs.before: Because I have a name and a face and a family on this block.
pairs.after: Because everybody on this block knows my face. I've got a kid.

pairs.speaker: lineman
pairs.before: Whoever is drinking that current does not like to be looked at. You are new here. You are cheaper to lose.
pairs.after: Whoever's drinking that current doesn't like being looked at. You're new. Nobody comes asking if you don't come back.

pairs.speaker: PLAYER
pairs.before: Comforting.
pairs.after: Comforting.

pairs.speaker: PLAYER
pairs.before: Who does not like to be looked at?
pairs.after: Who doesn't like being looked at?

pairs.speaker: lineman
pairs.before: If I knew that, I would not need you. Nobody who drinks that quiet keeps a name that stays put.
pairs.after: If I knew, I wouldn't need you. I asked my foreman about it once. He just looked at his hands till I stopped talking.

pairs.speaker: lineman
pairs.before: Follow the split. Do not make a show of it.
pairs.after: Follow the split. Don't make a show of it. Please.

pairs.speaker: lineman
pairs.before: Fair. It is nobody's job out here, which is why it is always nobody's job.
pairs.after: Yeah. Fair. I'll go ask somebody else's kid to do it.

pairs.speaker: PLAYER
pairs.before: Maybe another night.
pairs.after: Maybe another night.

pairs.speaker: PLAYER
pairs.before: Fine. I will look.
pairs.after: Fine. I'll look.

pairs.speaker: lineman
pairs.before: Good. It splits somewhere past the dead storefronts. Follow the cable that runs warm.
pairs.after: Good. Splits somewhere past the dead storefronts. Warm cable. You'll feel it before you see it.

pairs.speaker: fixer
pairs.before: Easy. You found the tap. Most people never look at a warm cable twice.
pairs.after: Easy. Easy, easy. Don't touch that, it's live.

pairs.speaker: fixer
pairs.before: I move a little current where it is needed. The grid has no owner. I am just faster than the meter.
pairs.after: I don't steal it. I move it. The grid doesn't belong to anybody so there's nothing there to steal, I'm just faster than the meter. That's it.

pairs.speaker: fixer
pairs.before: Put it back and go home a quiet hero. Or make this loud. Loud is where it gets expensive for both of us.
pairs.after: So. Put it back and go home and nobody hears a thing about it, or make it loud. Which are you?

pairs.speaker: PLAYER
pairs.before: Put it back. Nobody hears it.
pairs.after: Put it back. Nobody hears it.

pairs.speaker: PLAYER
pairs.before: The trades should see this.
pairs.after: The trades should see this.

pairs.speaker: PLAYER
pairs.before: Whose current is it, really?
pairs.after: Whose current is it?

pairs.speaker: PLAYER
pairs.before: (cut the tap, right now)
pairs.after: (cut the tap, right now)

pairs.speaker: fixer
pairs.before: See, that is the question that costs. I do not know whose.
pairs.after: Huh. That's the one question, isn't it. I don't know whose. Never have.

pairs.speaker: fixer
pairs.before: I know it goes down, not up. Toward the water. I do not follow it down and neither should you.
pairs.after: It runs down. Not up. Down, toward the water. That's where I quit asking and you should quit there too.

pairs.speaker: fixer
pairs.before: I gave you nothing. Put it back, or do not. Your block, your name.
pairs.after: I told you nothing. Understand me. Put it back or don't, it's your block and it's your face they'll remember.

pairs.speaker: PLAYER
pairs.before: Put it back. Quietly.
pairs.after: Put it back. Quietly.

pairs.speaker: PLAYER
pairs.before: Cut it. Let them all see.
pairs.after: Cut it. Let them see.

pairs.speaker: lineman
pairs.before: Light is back. I did not ask how.
pairs.after: Light's back. I'm not going to ask how.

pairs.speaker: lineman
pairs.before: You did not make a show of it. That is worth more out here than you will understand for a few years.
pairs.after: You didn't make a show of it. I noticed. Not going to say anything else about it.

pairs.speaker: PLAYER
pairs.before: Just fixed a line.
pairs.after: Just fixed a line.

pairs.speaker: lineman
pairs.before: You brought it to us instead of eating it yourself. Good. We patch it in the open.
pairs.after: You brought it to us. Could've kept it to yourself and you didn't.

pairs.speaker: lineman
pairs.before: They will know a crew looked, and looked together. That is its own kind of loud, but it is ours.
pairs.after: We patch it in daylight. Names on the work order, mine first, then the crew, then yours if you want it up there.

pairs.speaker: PLAYER
pairs.before: Do it in daylight.
pairs.after: Do it in daylight.

pairs.speaker: lineman
pairs.before: You cut it in front of everyone. Half the block cheered and the other half went very quiet.
pairs.after: You cut it in front of everybody. Somebody's kid was clapping. Nobody's mother was.

pairs.speaker: lineman
pairs.before: They felt that upstream. Whoever drinks that current now knows your face. I hope the light was worth it.
pairs.after: They felt that upstream. Somebody up there has your face now. I don't know what else to tell you.

pairs.speaker: PLAYER
pairs.before: Let them know my face.
pairs.after: Let them know my face.

pairs.speaker: PLAYER
pairs.before: (say nothing)
pairs.after: (say nothing)
